executive_summary: The Q2 platform migration carries medium overall risk driven by staffing constraints, undocumented API edge cases, and an aggressive timeline with no slack beyond a two-week buffer. Three enterprise clients on legacy webhooks create contractual exposure, and no single DRI has been assigned for client communication. The fraud detection v2 descoping requires compliance sign-off that has not been obtained.

risks.title: Platform API spec gaps threaten migration timeline
evidence_quotes: The new platform API isn't fully documented yet. We've been discovering edge cases in the batch processing layer that aren't covered in the spec.
If we hit more undocumented edge cases in batch processing, that two-week buffer evaporates fast.
risks.impact: Undocumented edge cases in batch processing could consume the entire two-week buffer, pushing delivery past June 30 into Q3 and creating a leadership reporting problem.
risks.mitigation: Dana's spike by Thursday to catalog known spec gaps. If the gap count is high, escalate immediately to re-scope or extend the timeline before sprint planning Monday.

risks.title: Staffing trade-off between platform migration and fraud detection v2
evidence_quotes: I only have three engineers on platform right now — one is already allocated to the observability rollout.
If I move someone, that slips.
Compliance has been breathing down our necks — they want it before the audit window opens May 1st.
risks.impact: Moving one engineer from payments to platform delays fraud detection v2, potentially missing the May 1 compliance audit window. Not moving the engineer leaves platform understaffed for dual webhook support.
risks.mitigation: Resolve the compliance conversation on fraud detection v2 descoping this week. Get explicit sign-off from compliance before reallocating the engineer.

risks.title: Enterprise client webhook migration lacks a DRI
evidence_quotes: Who owns the client communication about the webhook deprecation? Product or engineering?
We need a single DRI or this will stall.
Let's figure out the DRI offline.
risks.impact: Without a designated owner, client communication about the 90-day deprecation window stalls. Delayed client notification compresses their migration timeline, increasing the risk of contract disputes or emergency support escalations.
risks.mitigation: Assign a DRI for webhook deprecation communication before Thursday's reconvene. Do not wait for offline resolution — set a deadline.

unresolved_tensions.tension: Clean webhook cutover vs. dual-format support during transition
sides: Dana Okafor advocates clean cut to reduce testing surface and engineering burden
Leo Petrov argues enterprise clients with active contracts need a migration window
evidence_quotes: I'd strongly recommend we do a clean cut. Supporting both webhook formats doubles our integration testing surface.
If we cut them off without a migration window, we're looking at contract issues. Sales flagged this last week.
unresolved_tensions.why_it_matters: The group leaned toward 90-day dual support, but Dana never explicitly agreed — she stated the staffing cost. If the extra engineer doesn't materialize, this tension resurfaces as a blocker.

hidden_assumptions.assumption: One additional engineer from payments is sufficient to support dual webhook paths through Q2
hidden_assumptions.risk_if_false: If dual webhook support requires more than one engineer-quarter of effort, the platform team is still understaffed and the June 30 target is unachievable regardless of the buffer.
evidence_quotes: Leo, could you lend one engineer from payments to platform for the quarter?
That means my team is maintaining two paths through all of Q2.

hidden_assumptions.assumption: Compliance will accept a descoped fraud detection v2 with only critical rules
hidden_assumptions.risk_if_false: If compliance rejects the descope, the payments engineer cannot be reallocated, leaving the platform team at three engineers with one on observability — effectively two engineers for the migration.
evidence_quotes: We could descope fraud detection v2 to ship the critical rules only and push the ML-based scoring to Q3.
That's a conversation I'd need to have with the compliance team. I don't want to commit to that without their sign-off.

decision_gaps.missing_decision: Who is the DRI for webhook deprecation client communication?
decision_gaps.blocker: Three teams (product, engineering, sales) share partial ownership. Without a single DRI, no one initiates the 90-day deprecation clock with enterprise clients.

decision_gaps.missing_decision: Has compliance approved the fraud detection v2 descope?
decision_gaps.blocker: The staffing reallocation from payments to platform depends on this approval. Without it, the migration staffing plan is unconfirmed.

recommended_actions.action: Complete API spec gap spike and deliver findings to the team
recommended_actions.success_artifact: Written catalog of known undocumented edge cases in the batch processing layer, with severity estimates

recommended_actions.action: Get compliance sign-off on fraud detection v2 descope (critical rules only, ML scoring deferred to Q3)
recommended_actions.success_artifact: Written confirmation from compliance team accepting the descoped deliverable and revised timeline

recommended_actions.action: Assign a single DRI for webhook deprecation client communication and publish a RACI
recommended_actions.success_artifact: Named DRI with documented responsibilities for product messaging, technical migration guide, and sales outreach

recommended_actions.action: Notify Meridian Partners and enterprise clients of 90-day webhook deprecation window once DRI is assigned
recommended_actions.success_artifact: Sent deprecation notice to all affected clients with migration guide and support contact
